subject: Re: MAP & evaluation timeline — staged commit + renewal uplift discussion
messages:
From: Jessica Park <jessica.park@acme.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP kickoff + evaluation scope and commercial anchors

Hi Marissa & Rishi,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the routing controls. We'd like to formalize a short Mutual Action Plan so we can align internal stakeholders (infra, security, procurement) and lock an evaluation window. High-level asks from our side: 

- A 6-week evaluation (POC) with a dedicated instance that mirrors our anticipated 50 QPS peak.
- Access to KV/prefix caching and metrics export for our telemetry.
- A clear commercial anchor: what commit (monthly QPS or usage) would get us to a 20% discount on unit pricing?
- Renewal/expansion language: we want a staged commit so we can ramp, but need clarity on how renewal pricing adjusts if our usage grows faster than committed (uplift).

Can you share a draft MAP and the commercial milestones your team expects for a close? Also cc'ing Tom (platform lead) who will own the POC runbook.

Attachments: none on our side — will review any docs you send.

Best,
Jessica Park
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corporation
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Jessica Park <jessica.park@acme.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff + evaluation scope and commercial anchors

Jessica — thanks, and great to meet Tom last week.

Attached is a proposed MAP (20251103-Acme-MAP-v1.pdf) and a short commercial worksheet (20251110-Redwood-Proposal.xlsx). Summary below to keep things actionable: 

Mutual Action Plan (6-week POC) — key milestones:
1) Week 0 (kickoff): provisioning of a dedicated staged instance, ingress keys, baseline dashboard access.
2) Week 1–2 (load validation): run supplied traffic, confirm latency SLOs and cache hit rates.
3) Week 3–4 (integration): telemetry ingestion + function/tool-calling tests.
4) Week 5 (eval review): joint scorecard (latency, cost per token, error rate).
5) Week 6 (decision): ACME provides written decision: proceed to staged-commit or walk away.

Commercial anchors (initial proposal):
- Staged-commit for Q1: 50 committed QPS equivalent (monthly commitment) — price tier A.
- If signed within 30 days of successful eval: 20% off list unit price for the initial 12-month term.
- Ramp schedule: commitment unlocks burst capacity; production ramp gated by weekly telemetry review.

Renewal / uplift mechanics (draft):
- At renewal, committed baseline will be re-assessed. If average trailing-3-month usage exceeds committed baseline by >25%, an uplift applies to the overage at the next tier's unit price.
- If ACME commits to a 12‑month growth ramp (documented in the MAP with milestones), we can include an uplift cap (max +10% unit price on renewal) and an incentive credit tied to on-time ramp milestones.

Open items for negotiation: exact QPS-to-commit mapping, measurement window for uplift, and the discount cadence (one-time vs. step-down during term).

Next steps: 
- Can Tom share the runbook and a sample traffic file by Thursday?
- Rishi, can you confirm whether we can offer the renewal uplift cap (max +10%) as a standard line item or whether we need legal to review?

Thanks — attaching the MAP and the worksheet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: 20251103-Acme-MAP-v1.pdf, 20251110-Redwood-Proposal.xlsx
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, Jessica Park <jessica.park@acme.com>
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 08:24:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff + evaluation scope and commercial anchors

Marissa + Jessica — quick commercial clarification to surface before Tom starts the runbook: 

1) Commit sizing: we typically express commit as a token/month equivalent or a committed QPS bucket. For this MAP, 50 QPS sustained for peak windows maps to ~1.2B tokens/month (approx). If ACME signs 50 QPS committed baseline, the example pricing below applies:
   - List unit price: $0.006/token (example)
   - Close-time incentive: 20% off unit price on signed 12-month commitment following a successful POC.

2) Renewal uplift construct (negotiable):
   - Trailing-3-month average usage measured against committed baseline. If >25% overage, uplift is charged on the delta at a blended uplift rate (we propose +8% on base unit price).
   - If customer documents a ramp plan inside the MAP (weeks + expected QPS increases), and hits ramp milestones on schedule, we are prepared to cap uplift to +4% on the delta for the next renewal.

3) Credits & rollback: if we miss our SLOs during the first 3 months of production, ACME is eligible for service credits that can offset uplift charges at renewal (subject to SLO-impact review).

Legal note: anything that caps uplift or ties uplift to milestone credits will need to be in the SOW and flagged for legal review.

I'll join the kickoff call to explain measurement windows.

-Rishi
VP Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: contracts@acme.com

Date: Thu, 28 Jan 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MAP & evaluation timeline — redlines and questions

Marissa, Rishi — attached are a couple of redlines and a few questions from Acme Legal after reviewing the MAP and the proposed commercial worksheet. Summary: 

- Need stronger clarity on uplift measurement: specify the exact metric (trailing-90-day daily average vs. trailing-3-month arithmetic mean).
- Request an uplift cap option (we prefer a hard cap of +6% on renewal uplift).
- Ask for KMS/HSM assurance and confirmation that audit logs for inference requests are retained for 12 months.
- Request a staged signature approach: execute the SOW for Stage 1 (12 weeks), then sign Stage 2 SOW after milestone acceptance.

See attached: Acme_Redlines_20260128.pdf. Can Redwood provide updated wording for the uplift metric and the audit log/KMS commitments? Also confirm whether the proposed DocuSign flow can be staged (we prefer not to sign all stages at once).

Regards,
Acme Contracts
Acme Corporation
Attachments: Acme_Redlines_20260128.pdf
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: contracts@acme.com, Jessica Park <jessica.park@acme.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 19:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MAP & evaluation timeline — staged SOW acceptance and final commercial terms

Acme contracts / Jessica — thanks for the review and solid feedback. Quick update and proposal to close: 

1) Measurement window: we will use trailing-90-day rolling average of daily usage (tokens/day) to determine uplift deltas. We'll include precise calculation language in the SOW.
2) Uplift cap: Redwood can accept a negotiated uplift cap of +6% (final) provided ACME commits to a staged SOW approach with the following milestones and credits:
   - Stage 1 (12 weeks): POC + integration — on acceptance, Stage 1 invoiced at committed tier with 20% close incentive.
   - Stage 2 (12 months): production term — baseline commit established at Stage 1 accepted level. If trailing-90-day average at renewal > baseline +25%, uplift up to +6% applies to delta.
   - If Redwood misses SLOs that materially impact the deployment (as defined in the SLO appendix), ACME will receive service credits that offset up to 50% of uplift charges at renewal.
3) Security: confirmation — KMS support for customer-managed keys and 12-month audit log retention for inference request metadata are available in Private and Dedicated modes; we'll include the option in the SOW and reference the audit log export process.
4) DocuSign: we can do staged signing. SOW will be structured so Stage 1 signs now; Stage 2 DocuSign envelope goes live on acceptance.

Next step: I'll have Legal build the precise uplift and measurement language into the SOW and send a DocuSign envelope for Stage 1 by EOD Monday. If that works, Rishi and I will proceed to finalize pricing in the worksheet and prepare an approval note for the CS handoff.

Thanks — appreciate the clear asks.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
